change: A single higher-resolution viewport image is captured after settling, transformed on zoom, and replaced by sharp live SVG. Capture misses never wait; PNG encoding runs on a bounded background worker.

priorMatchedNativePair.status: Earlier implementation; final comparison below uses the current helper, completion notification and decoded-element reuse.

experiments.reason: Incorrect physical fit-scale readiness caused zero snapshots and zero hits; mandatory enabled-mode cache-hit checks were added.
Hiding dense SVG during the transition increased median ten-step zoom to 5604 ms and last-input-to-ready latency to 1146 ms; live SVG is retained under the image.
Two handoff RAFs had 437 ms median final-ready latency; removed one unnecessary handoff frame.
Desktop locked during the optimized build. Final run used a temporary keep-awake assertion; no permanent sleep-setting changes.

Partial native captures passed but full mode had zero idle captures because final completion occurred after DOM mutations. Added a completion hook and failing-before/passing-after deterministic regression.
Both viewer cache checks passed; native End stayed at page 0 after full zoom/fit. Explicit Home/End navigation now works in both viewers and preserves text-field and modified keys.

nativeInteraction.scope: Native mouse and keyboard input in the composed editor; actual build/backend, read-only DOM/geometry and cache counters checked. No composed-window pixel or physical trackpad-pinch claim.

visualInspection.scope: Fresh standalone WKWebView image of the production helper cache transform at1.4x, with the underlying SVG left unchanged; a deterministic visual scene, not a physical input or composed-editor screenshot.

limitations: Standalone optimized Swift WKWebView probe uses the production JavaScript helper with a Cocoa PNG capture provider. The app uses the Rust background TIFF-to-PNG worker; their encoder timings are not interchangeable.
Last-input latency measures matching DOM readiness and RAF handoff, not final GPU presentation or physical trackpad pinch.
Warmed active workloads on one arm64 macOS14.6.1 desktop in low-power mode; no cross-platform, cold-startup or idle CPU guarantee.
Dense full-rendering capacity still exceeds the earlier bounded probe budget; native full-mode interaction coverage uses the standard48-page fixture.

Final current-helper comparison: ten-step sequence median 4052 ms disabled versus 3520 ms enabled (13.1% shorter), but last-input-to-sharp-ready median 415 ms versus 447 ms (32 ms longer). Worst zoom RAF gaps remain about 0.67 seconds. Temporary feedback improves; final SVG rendering is not faster.
Very large viewports can reach the four-million-pixel cap at lower density than the physical display. The higher-resolution target is best-effort within the fixed budget.
